summary: Frontend-only iteration 19 verification passed all requested title-animation-removal and HUD regression checks on the public URL. After boot was skipped, h1[data-testid='sirius-title'] was immediately visible as one plain ΣIRIUS text node with zero child elements/spans; no .sirius-title-letter nodes or letterIn keyframes existed. Its computed animation-name was exactly 'goldSheen, goldPulse'. Across seven samples over 13 seconds, title geometry changed by 0.000 px and opacity, transform, clip-path, and readability remained stable. Both hand assets were visible at mid-height, and the command bar accepted, submitted, and cleared input with a rendered response.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested title and quick HUD regression checks passed

seed_data_creation: No backend data created. Browser localStorage was populated with the requested Testeur/Paris profile, current briefing date and PWA dismissal timestamp; installed/hands flags and the session WAHOU flag suppressed unrelated overlays during the 13-second observation.
context_for_next_testing_agent: At 1920x1080, the title innerHTML was exactly ΣIRIUS with a single text child node, zero spans globally, opacity 1, white-space nowrap, clip-path none, transform none, and animation-name 'goldSheen, goldPulse'. Its rect stayed x=606.47, y=284.25, width=723.08, height=264.00 for all samples at 2/4/6/8/10/12/13 seconds. Both 1024px hand assets loaded and centered near y=540. The command 'quelle heure est-il' cleared the input and returned a local spoken-time subtitle. There were no page errors, visible DOM errors, or title-related console errors. Six bounded ws://localhost:8765 connection failures were the previously documented public-preview behavior and unrelated to this change.
rca_of_the_issue: The overlap risk was removed at its source: the title is rendered as one plain text node instead of independently animated per-letter spans, and the letterIn animation/class are absent. Runtime verification confirmed only the intentional goldSheen and goldPulse animations remain, so no animation modifies individual letter opacity or position.
